headline: National Security Bureau accuses China of six tactics interfering in nine-in-one local elections incl. discounted airfares
dek: NSB accuses the CCP of six interference tactics ahead of the nine-in-one local elections: illicit financial assistance to candidates, subsidised trips to China, discounted flights to bring Taiwanese residents in China home to vote (available ~3 weeks before polling), disinformation, illegal…
sources: Taiwan NSB Director-General Tsai Ming-yen (legislature briefing); Taipei Times
fault_line: Defensive disclosure or election narrative? Taipei says Beijing is buying votes with discounted flights; Beijing is silent.

sections.what_happened: NSB accuses the CCP of six interference tactics ahead of the nine-in-one local elections: illicit financial assistance to candidates, subsidised trips to China, discounted flights to bring Taiwanese residents in China home to vote (available ~3 weeks before polling), disinformation, illegal underground betting, cyberattacks for sensitive election data. NSB reports Government Service Network recorded an average of ~2.58M intrusion attempts daily as of September, with 100M+ attempts in July. Separately, Taiwan is probing organized-crime links to China's 'transnational repression' (prior-covered, sig 1).
sections.what_verified: NSB legislative report via Taipei Times; Beijing did not respond to comment requests on parallel grey-zone escalation claims (tradersunion Oct 22)
sections.what_disputed: China did not respond to requests for comment; the accusation comes from the side running the elections
sections.why_matters: Attribute strictly to Taiwan's NSB; the number carries the card: 2.58M intrusion attempts per day. Coherence: pair with the $14B arms-sale holdup — Taiwan under pressure on two fronts, ballot and battlefield.
sections.context: Background: Taiwan — NEW (Oct 22): National Security Bureau accuses China of six tactics interfering in nine-in-one local elections incl. discounted airfares, disinfo, 2.58M daily cyber intrusions

totw_analysis: Our read: Attribute strictly to Taiwan's NSB; the number carries the card: 2.58M intrusion attempts per day. Coherence: pair with the $14B arms-sale holdup — Taiwan under pressure on two fronts, ballot and battlefield. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Defensive disclosure or election narrative? Taipei says Beijing is buying votes with discounted flights; Beijing is silent.
